title: Ordinary Zariski module pushforward preserves filtered colimits
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], meaning inverse images of affine opens are quasi-compact and the diagonal of $f$ is quasi-compact. Let $I$ be a small nonempty filtered category and $M:I\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ a diagram of sheaves of modules on the Zariski topology [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. With $f_*$ the ordinary module pushforward [def-pc-module-pullback], the canonical comparison $\operatorname{colim}_{j\in I}f_*M_j\longrightarrow f_*(\operatorname{colim}_{j\in I}M_j)$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Tag 07TB (lemma-colimit-cohomology), p=0; the module form is the same underlying abelian-sheaf comparison with its natural structure-sheaf action.

proof.text: Put $L=\operatorname{colim}_I M_j$ in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ and $C=\operatorname{colim}_I f_*M_j$ in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y)$, with coprojections $a_j$ and $b_j$. These colimits exist, and their underlying abelian sheaves are the corresponding colimits of underlying abelian sheaves, by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](2),(3). The cocone $f_*a_j$ induces the canonical module morphism $c:C\to f_*L$, characterized by $c b_j=f_*a_j$.

source.place: Tag 07TB, lemma-colimit-cohomology, proof, specialized to p=0; sections argument via Sites Tag 0738.

proof.text: Fix an affine open $V\subseteq Y$ and put $W=f^{-1}V=X\times_YV$. The affine scheme $V$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Base change preserves quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3), so $W\to V$ has both properties. Part (2) of that same node gives that $W$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-cofinal-finite-coverings] separately to $V$ and $W$: every open cover of either is refined by a finite affine open cover whose pairwise intersections are quasi-compact. These are also covers in the ambient opens sites of $Y$ and $X$, respectively; an open of an open subspace is an ambient open, with exactly the same coverings and intersections.

source.place: Tag 07TB, lemma-colimit-cohomology, proof, specialized to p=0; sections argument via Sites Tag 0738.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-site-quasi-compact-section-colimit] to the underlying abelian-sheaf diagrams on the opens sites of $Y$ and $X$, at the objects $V$ and $W$ respectively. Its small filtered index hypothesis is exactly the hypothesis on $I$, and its cofinal finite-cover hypothesis was checked in step 2. With the colimit identifications of step 1 this gives isomorphisms of abelian groups $\alpha_V:\operatorname{colim}_I(f_*M_j)(V)\xrightarrow{\sim}C(V)$ and $\beta_W:\operatorname{colim}_I M_j(W)\xrightarrow{\sim}L(W)$, induced by $b_j(V)$ and $a_j(W)$. No global quasi-separatedness of $Y$ or $X$ is required by the cited sections lemma.

source.place: Tag 07TB, lemma-colimit-cohomology, proof, specialized to p=0; sections argument via Sites Tag 0738.

proof.text: By the definition of ordinary module pushforward, $(f_*M_j)(V)=M_j(W)$ and $(f_*L)(V)=L(W)$; the scalar action is through $\mathcal O_Y(V)\to\mathcal O_X(W)$. Under this identity of the two section diagrams, $c(V)\alpha_V=\beta_W$: after each colimit coprojection both maps are $a_j(W)$, by $c b_j=f_*a_j$, and equality follows from the colimit universal property. Thus $c(V)$ is bijective for every affine open $V$. The affine opens form a basis by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], so [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis](b), applied to the underlying abelian sheaves, makes $c$ an isomorphism there. Its inverse is also a module morphism: for each open, bijectivity and $c(r x)=r c(x)$ give $c^{-1}(r y)=r c^{-1}(y)$, and the inverse commutes with restrictions by the same cancellation. By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] this is an inverse in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y)$, as required.
